hero.headline: Build unmissable products, services, and experiences that earn a place in people's lives.
hero.subhead: I work with product, growth, and marketing leaders who need a clearer point of view on customer value, experience, and how their products or services should evolve.

fitPoints: Engagement, retention, or repeat usage has plateaued
Customer expectations in your category are shifting
Your product or experience works, but no longer feels distinctive
Your brand promise is stronger than what the experience currently delivers
There's pressure to evolve, but not enough clarity on where the real opportunity is
You need a stronger read on what customers will value next

problemFraming.eyebrow: Why Experience-Led Growth Is Needed Now More Than Ever
problemFraming.heading: From Share Of Attention To Share Of Life
problemFraming.body: I think more organizations need to shift from chasing attention to earning a real place in people's lives. That's what I mean by Experience-Led Growth: creating business value by becoming more useful, more relevant, and more worth returning to over time.

cards.title: Trust Is Distributed
cards.description: People don’t make decisions based on brand messaging alone. They’re checking Reddit, group chats, reviews, creators, and LLMs that don’t agree. You have less control over how people form opinions and decide what’s worth choosing.

cards.title: Attention Isn't Relationship
cards.description: Reach can get you seen. It doesn’t guarantee relevance. Experience-Led Growth is about building enough value that people return because they want to.

cards.title: Expectations Became Liquid
cards.description: What people want from a product or service now moves across categories faster than most organizations are built to respond to. What feels novel quickly becomes baseline.

cards.title: Utility Has To Justify The Ask
cards.description: People are more aware of what they’re giving up now: their data, time, attention, and trust. If you’re asking for any of those things, the value in return has to be obvious in the experience itself.
